predecessors.name: Kalabhra dynasty
predecessors.text: the Pandya core of Cliopatria: Madurai, Tirunelveli and southern Kerala, c.

successors.name: Chola Empire
successors.text: Madurai and the Pandya country: Parantaka I 'completed his conquest of the entire Pandya country'

ledger.x: c. 765: Varagunavarman I takes Kongu. 'Invaded the Pallava country and conquered the Kongu country' (reign c. 765-815); the page gives no year for the conquest, so the start of his reign is used.
c. 897: Kongu goes to the Cholas. 'By c. 897 CE, Chola king Aditya I was the master of the old Pallava, Ganga and Kongu countries'. The year is the page's 'c. 897'.

c. 915: the Pandya king loses at Vellur. 'The decisive battle appears to have taken place at Vellur around 915'; 'this victory was narrow'; Parantaka 'completed his conquest of the entire Pandya country' (undated). The occupation turns into annexation.
c. 915: the Pandya kingdom is conquered. 'Then the Pandya king fled into exile in Sri Lanka'. Cliopatria runs the row to 921.

wars.name: Pandya conquest of Kongu
wars.outcome: Varagunavarman I conquered the Kongu country; it passed to the Cholas by c.

wars.name: Pandya-Sinhalese wars of the 9th century
wars.outcome: Srimara Srivallabha (815-862) 'sailed to Sri Lanka, subjugated and overpowered King Sena I' (undated); Sena II then 'invaded the Pandya country, sacked Madurai' (undated) and Varaguna II was chosen king; Varaguna II suffered a crushing defeat near Kumbakonam…

wars.name: Chola conquest of the Pandya country
wars.outcome: Parantaka I captured Madurai in 910 and won the decisive battle at Vellur c.

certainty.note: The page gives regions and reigns only; the Kongu and Venad limits are reigns, not borders.
